articles.title: Poetic Biography
articles.subtitle: The story behind the breath you didn’t know you were holding.
articles.summary: I’m not just a lover. I’m a storm you call by name. I don’t slip softly into places or people. I arrive like a confession you never meant to make, & when I leave, I take a piece of you with me, while leaving a piece of myself, still burning, behind.
articles.description: The story behind the breath you didn’t know you were holding.

articles.title: The Guild: A Chronicle of Pretty Souls
articles.subtitle: A myth-bent memory of digital devotion, told in glitch-forged rhyme & frosting-slick fire.
articles.summary:
A digital elegy for joy, grief, and the guild that made it all sacred.

This story is a reimagined myth built from real memories. Every section is rooted in lived experience from my time leading a guild in a fantasy MMO, where connection was forged through gameplay, laughter, late nights, and digital stillness.
articles.description: A myth-bent memory of digital devotion, told in glitch-forged rhyme & frosting-slick fire.

articles.title: Cold Children
articles.subtitle: They never grew old. That was the gift and the warning.
articles.summary:
The Hook

They keep her behind glass now.

The room is quiet. Not sterile, just reverent. Lights dimmed to mimic dusk. A few chairs along the far wall, each facing her enclosure like pews.
articles.description: They never grew old. That was the gift and the warning.

articles.title: Lanterns for the Unreturning
articles.subtitle: A forgotten letter. A love unstilled by time. A voice carried only by memory.
articles.summary:
The Invocation

To the one whose voice was once the wind through bamboo,

I write by oillight, though the wick is old and the flame pulls toward the open window. Outside, the plum trees bend under spring’s last chill, and the paper screens tremble as if remembering you. I know you will not read this. Perhaps you no longer walk this world. Perhaps you live, and have forgotten me. But I have not forgotten you.
articles.description: A forgotten letter. A love unstilled by time. A voice carried only by memory.

articles.title: The Khan Who Chose the Grain
articles.subtitle: A legend reborn in mercy, where empire was traded for grain & silence grew into legacy.
articles.summary:
The Scroll in the Dust

They say the sky chose him.

Before the legends, before the fear, he was only Temujin, a boy born beneath a cracked moon, his mother’s cry louder than the wolves outside the firelight.
articles.description: A legend reborn in mercy, where empire was traded for grain & silence grew into legacy.

articles.title: Eggasaurus Rex
articles.subtitle: In the Land of Wobblebottom, nothing rolls quite like him...
articles.summary:
-Author’s Note from the Wobbleverse.

This wobbly, glitter-splattered tale is a joyful break from my usual writing. Eggasaurus Rex is my very first attempt at a children’s short story, filled with sock trees, meatball disasters, and one delightfully ridiculous hero. I'd say it's meant for kids somewhere under the age of 9.

articles.title: Where We Last Were Us
articles.subtitle: Two voices. One place. Never again the same.
articles.summary:
Quiet. Poetic. Told entirely in dialogue between two voices echoing through a shared past.

This is a story about what we keep, what we lose, and the places that remember us even when we don’t return.
articles.description: Two voices. One place. Never again the same.

articles.title: Before the Sky Went Quiet: Part I - The Girl Who Faded
articles.subtitle: When her voice began to disappear, everything else followed.
articles.summary:
Chapter One

If You’re Reading This

The attic still smelled like her shampoo. Lavender and citrus. Too bright. Too alive. The kind that clung to blankets and door frames and memories that refused to leave quietly.
articles.description: When her voice began to disappear, everything else followed.

articles.title: Before the Sky Went Quiet: Part II - The Goodbye
articles.subtitle: She chose how she would leave. They chose how they’d remember her.
articles.summary:
Chapter Seven

The Last Clear Day

She knew the second she opened her eyes.

This was her last real day.

No pain.

No confusion.
articles.description: She chose how she would leave. They chose how they’d remember her.

articles.title: Before the Sky Went Quiet: Part III - The Echo That Stayed
articles.subtitle: She’s gone. But the sound of her hasn’t left.
articles.summary:
Chapter Ten

The Letter She Never Sent

Mae didn’t cry at the funeral.

She sat in the third row with her hands folded tight in her lap, watching the slideshow like she was trying to memorize every photo before it disappeared.
articles.description: She’s gone. But the sound of her hasn’t left.
